title: Stakes
brief: Invent one new widget that goes beyond everything in the catalog. One remarkable idea, or none.

stamps.reason: The same idea as Squiggle in this round, minus the paint in the prompt box and the fix on click, so it is the weaker variation of its own sibling.
stamps.subject: Pointer

stamps.reason: Deciding which hedges the reply 'addressed' by a phrase list and word overlap will be wrong often enough that the card cannot be trusted, and it has nothing to read when thinking is off or summarised.
stamps.subject: Doubt

stamps.reason: A narrow cut of insight-widget (prompting habits against turn outcomes) with a coloured word added; the inventor ranked it last for the same reason.
stamps.subject: Famous Last Words

stamps.reason: Not chosen: a charming read of the thinking stream, but it gives the person nothing to act on and is empty whenever thinking is off or summarised.
stamps.subject: Second Thoughts

stamps.reason: Not chosen: new and funny once, but it keeps what the person chose to delete, changes no decision, and cannot yet tell a swallowed draft from history recall or a cleared box.
stamps.subject: Unsent

stamps.reason: Not chosen: useful, but it rests on parsing lsof and netstat per platform every turn and on killing processes by pid, a heavier and riskier build than Stakes for a quieter payoff.
stamps.subject: Strays

stamps.reason: Not chosen: the strongest runner-up, but picking out which typed words are meant as file or branch names will misfire, and @-completion already covers the path case; worth a later order.
stamps.subject: Squiggle

stamps.reason: Not chosen: a real new interaction, but it works only in fullscreen, needs a second command and one command per note, and helps less often than a line under every destructive permission dialog.
stamps.subject: Margin

stamps.reason: Stakes is the only idea that changes a decision the person makes alone: it measures what a yes would lose and writes it into the permission dialog, which no widget touches, with every call it needs present in the types file.
The spec meets the standard, every hook and call it names is in the types file, all main states are drawn and it reads at 20 columns; 12 notes for the machinist.
Built stakes-widget: a Bash tool.check hook that measures five destructive command shapes with read-only git probes, writes one line under the dialog and keeps the last five verdicts on the card.

Two wrong lines under the dialog: rm -rf .git (and rm -rf . in a clean tree) reads 'Nothing lost', and git push -f origin HEAD measures origin/HEAD instead of the pushed branch; both must become 'unrecognised form' with tests in A6 and A5. See inspection.md findings 1 and 2.

Fixed inspection findings 1 and 2: rm of .git, a path under it, or a path that holds the repository (., .., /) and git push -f to HEAD, @ or a ^ or ~ branch word now read unrecognised form with no probe, tested in A6 and A5.

Acting on the inspector's held finding: rm -rf of the repository's absolute path, or of a path with a .. segment, reads Nothing lost while it deletes .git. Such paths must read unrecognised form unless shown to lie strictly below the top level; add tests in A6.

Fixed inspection finding 1: rm of a path with a .. segment, or of an absolute path not shown by rev-parse --show-toplevel to lie strictly below the top level, now reads unrecognised form with no ls-files probe, tested in A6; a verdict word longer than the card is now broken inside the border, tested in A15.

The spec's rm line 'Nothing lost: no files there' is written when git lists nothing, but git lists nothing for a path in the wrong case on Windows and macOS (rm -rf SRC) and for a file inside a nested repository or worktree, so it appears under commands that delete real work; with U and T zero the widget must confirm the path is absent or say Could not measure, and a nested repository must not count as 1 file. See inspection.md findings 1, 2 and 5.

The three faults of the send-back are answered (an --error-unmatch probe gives 'git sees no files there', a nested repository or submodule gives 'holds another repository', probes follow classic.CwdChanged), every call named is in the types file and nothing in the changes blocks; 17 notes for the machinist.

Rebuilt rm to the new spec: an --error-unmatch probe gives 'git sees no files there' (no more 'Nothing lost: no files there'), a nested repository or submodule gives 'holds another repository', absolute paths go to git under the top level's own text, and probes follow classic.CwdChanged; tested in A6, A8 and A11.

The build matches the spec and standard, the third-pass faults are fixed, and 90 commands driven through the real hook against real git gave no false 'Nothing lost'; the line under a live dialog is still unseen and the director should look at one before shipping.
On the demo page, in the README and the marketplace; smoke test clean
